description: Use SIMD shuffle-based lookup tables (PSHUFB/TBL) to classify every byte in a 16/32/64-byte chunk into one of several categories (delimiter, quote, newline, whitespace, other) in a single instruction, replacing multi-branch switch statements.
mathematical_formalization: f: byte -> {COMMA, QUOTE, NEWLINE, CR, OTHER}. Implemented as: low_nibble = byte & 0x0F, high_nibble = byte >> 4. class = LUT_low[low_nibble] & LUT_high[high_nibble]. 2 PSHUFB + 1 AND per 16 bytes = 0.1875 instructions/byte.
analogical_connections: Perfect hashing for small character sets
FPGA look-up tables implementing arbitrary boolean functions
Bloom filter probing with two hash functions
implementation_hypothesis: For CSV, detect comma (0x2C), quote (0x22), LF (0x0A), CR (0x0D). Construct two 16-byte LUTs indexed by nibble. AND results for exact match. Extract per-class bitmasks.
experiment_seed: Benchmark vectorized classification vs. scalar switch on random bytes and real CSV. Measure instructions/byte and branch mispredictions.
